Loss-of-function mutations in C1QA lead to a deficiency in C1q, which is essential for the initiation of the classical complement pathway. Dysregulation of the complement system impairs immune responses, contributing to immunodeficiency. Simultaneously, CVID is associated with defects in various genes critical for B cell development and function (e.g., MS4A1, CR2, CD19, TNFRSF13C, IL21, IRF2BP2, ICOS, IKZF1, NFKB2, NFKB1, SEC61A1, TNFRSF13B, CD81, LRBA). The complement system, particularly through C1q, plays a role in B cell activation, antibody production, and clearance of immune complexes, thus interacting with and influencing B cell development and function. Therefore, a defect in C1q (C1q deficiency) can exacerbate or contribute to the immunodeficiency phenotype seen in CVID by disrupting this cross-talk.

partners.mechanism_chain: C1QB (HGNC:1892) —DISRUPTS→ Complement system activation (GO:0006955); MS4A1 (HGNC:24032) —DISRUPTS→ B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050851); Complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002714); B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050851) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002714); Complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Deficiency of plasma proteins (HP:0030186). Dysregulation in these pathways leads to recurrent infections and deficiencies in plasma proteins, representing phenotypic convergence.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in CFH in individuals with both CVID and basal laminar drusen, or demonstration that CFH variants in affected individuals have differential functional consequences in immune cells versus ocular tissues that cannot be explained by complement dysregulation. _(variant: presence of a common (AF > 0.01) pathogenic variant in CFH)_

#### 10. properdin deficiency, X-linked  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.393)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-977606)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in CFP (HGNC:1806) —DISRUPTS→ Complement Factor Properdin (CFP) (HGNC:1806); Complement Factor Properdin (CFP) (HGNC:1806) —DECREASES→ Complement Alternative Pathway Activation (GO:0009106); Complement Alternative Pathway Activation (GO:0009106) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired complement activation (HP:0030171); Impaired complement activation (HP:0030171) —LEADS_TO→ Properdin deficiency, X-linked (MONDO:0010713); Complement Alternative Pathway Activation (GO:0009106) —LEADS_TO→ B cell defect (HP:0003831); B cell defect (HP:0003831) —LEADS_TO→ Common variable immunodeficiency (MONDO:0015517). Loss-of-function variants in CFP disrupt the complement alternative pathway, leading to impaired complement activation and susceptibility to infections characteristic of properdin deficiency. This same pathway, or related signaling cascades involving complement components, can be dysregulated in some forms of CVID, potentially through shared downstream effects or alternative genetic hits impacting this pathway, leading to B cell defects.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for CVID and properdin deficiency, or a demonstration that CFP variants conferring properdin deficiency do not impact CVID phenotypes in relevant models, would falsify this hypothesis. Specifically, if mutations in other CVID-associated genes (e.g., ICOS, TNFRSFF13B) are found to operate entirely independently of CFP function and complement alternative pathway activation, this hypothesis would be weakened. _(variant: Discovery of common variants in CFP (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) that are associated with CVID would strongly support this hypothesis, while pathogenic variants for properdin deficiency are expected to be rare.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the overlap in complement system involvement could lead to targeted therapies for CVID patients with specific complement defects, potentially involving augmentation of complement function or modulation of downstream immune responses. It also highlights the importance of considering complement pathways in the broader context of primary immunodeficiencies.
